 Barcelona Femeni v Arsenal Preview
 Arsenal Women Arsenal Women Match Previews 
 Tim Stillman 
 November 11, 2026 
 5 
 THE LOWDOWN 
Arsenal play Barcelona at the Camp Nou in the Champions League league phase on Thursday at 5.45pm UK time. The match was originally set to take place on Wednesday but was moved back to Thursday evening due to a general strike taking place in Spain on Wednesday.
 It’s the first time the Gunners have squared up to Barcelona since the 2025 Champions League Final in Lisbon in 2025. That day represented the height of the Renee Slegers era. It’s fair to say that Slegers’ tenure has hit a resounding low since then. If victory in Lisbon 18 months ago was a surprise against an all conquering Barca team, victory on Thursday would represent a much bigger shock.
 It’s the first time Arsenal Women will play in the Camp Nou and any sort of result would represent an enormous boon for Arsenal’s faltering season, especially with a Champions League qualification six pointer at home to London City Lionesses on the horizon this weekend. It’s a make or break week for Renee Slegers and Arsenal.
 The Gunners also play at home to European heavyweights Lyon next week, it’s a trio of tough, season defining games. Arsenal are currently fifth in the league phase standings and if they want to break into the top four who avoid the round of 16 and immediately qualify for the quarter-finals, they need a couple of huge results.
 TEAM NEWS 
Ona Batlle travelled with the squad after missing Sunday’s win at Anfield. Stina Blackstenius is out with an achilles injury. Chloe Kelly is training on grass again after a hamstring injury but this game will come too soon for her. Daphne van Domselaar was not included in the Champions League squad list so will not be involved. Mariona (hamstring), Michelle Agyemang (knee), Katie Reid (ankle) and Selina Cerci (knee) are all out.

Forwards: 9.Foord 11.Smith 19.Baum 23.Russo 60.Dixon
 A WORD FROM THE BOSS 
‘We’re going to compete for points. Barcelona are the same, so I think it will be a great game of football. For us, like I said, performance and results, I believe, will go hand-in-hand. But definitely here in two days’ time to compete with Barcelona for the points. We know how good they are on the ball. We know that we have to be comfortable without the ball as well. That’s definitely part of the mindset.
 ‘A lot of the players in the squad have done it before. I think in that sense, what we faced against Liverpool was a team that was in possession more than our opponents normally. We normally dominate possession. But yes, no, huge respect. We will have to suffer. We’ll have to put bodies on the lines. We’ll have to be really disciplined. But then, in the same breath, saying that we have a lot of quality in our team as well.
 ‘So we want to boast our qualities and our threat onto Barcelona. I know about the connection of Barcelona with the fans. I know they’re really intense and loud. I remember it from the final. I coached one game at the Camp Nou several years ago. It’s a historic, fantastic stadium, so there will be a great atmosphere. We’re very proud to have, I think, 1,000 travelling fans from London as well. We’ll try to connect as much as possible with them as well. We’re always so privileged to play for our fans.’
 LAST TIME OUT 
The teams last met in the Champions League Final in Lisbon in may 2025, Arsenal won 1-0 thanks to a second half goal from Stina Blackstenius and The Gunners won the Champions League for the second time. They remain the only British team to have won the trophy.
 THE OPPOSITION 
Barca were wounded by that final defeat in 2025 and, in 2026, Barcelona did what Barcelona do. They went and won the trophy back, thumping Lyon 4-0 in the final in Oslo. There is no doubt that European women’s football is still firmly ensconced in its Barcelona era with the Catalan club having wrestled primacy away from Lyon.
 They underwent some change in the summer, with taliswoman and current Ballon D’Or holder Alexia Putellas and stalwart centre-half Mapi Leon both signing for London City Lionesses. Winger Salma Paralluelo also signed for Lyon, in return, Barca broke the bank for Brazilian winger Kerolin from Manchester City.
 But in true Barca style, their academy continues to produce world class talent to replenish their squad. Aitana Bonmati has been eased back in slowly following a knee injury but talent like Claudia Pina, Vicky Lopez, Patri and elite goal scorer Ewa Pajor buttress the team with emerging talents like Schertenleib and Clara Serrajordi set to trouble Ballon D’Or shortlists for years to come.
 PLAYER TO WATCH 
Leah Williamson’s performances so far this season have come in for some criticism among some sections of the fan base. My personal opinion is that that has been unfair. Arsenal’s defenders have all been exposed by a new high pressing system which has yet to truly ‘latch.’
 Every Arsenal defender has suffered as a result of this this season and players don’t all suddenly lose their ability at the same time. At Anfield on Sunday, when I watched the game back a second time, I was actually struck by how well Williamson played, she led the team for clearances, interceptions and passed into the final third 18 times, 10 more times than the player who managed it the second most times.
 When questioned about the England captain’s form last season, Renee Slegers recited a Dutch saying, ‘the high tree catches all the wind’ and I think that is often the case for Williamson. However, her and her goalkeeper and defenders are going to undergo an almighty test in Barcelona. The final in Lisbon was one of Williamson’s best displays in an Arsenal shirt and a similar performance will be required on Thursday.
 MY PREDICTED LINE UP 
 Subs: 3.Wubben-Moy 5.De Almeida 12.L.Maanum 14.Reuteler 24.Hinds 28.Borbe 31.Holmberg 32.Cooney-Cross 40.Damm 60.Dixon
 HOW TO CATCH THE GAME 
The game takes place at the Spotify Camp Nou on Thursday at 5.45pm UK time and 6.45pm local time. It will be shown live on Disney + in the UK. Full global listings are available here .
 COMING UP 
We are on the ground in Barcelona and will have all the usual coverage for you, with every word of Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference online around an hour after full-time. We will also have an opinion piece on the match afterwards. Don’t forget to subscribe to our free weekly Arsenal Women Newsletter .
